## AGI vs Superintelligence: The Difference, Explained

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/agi-vs-superintelligence
Last updated: July 10, 2026 · Updated as verdicts change

One is human-level breadth; the other is beyond-human everything. AGI is AI that can do essentially any cognitive task a skilled human can. Superintelligence (ASI) is AI far beyond the best humans at essentially everything. In the standard forecast they are links in a chain: AGI automates AI research, an intelligence explosion follows, and ASI is the result. As of mid-2026: AGI-by-2027 is Open; the explosion and ASI are Pending.

Q: What is the difference between AGI and superintelligence?
A: AGI matches skilled humans at general cognitive work; superintelligence (ASI) far exceeds the best humans at essentially everything. AGI is the trigger; ASI is the predicted result of AGI automating AI research.

Q: Does AGI come before superintelligence?
A: In every major forecast, yes. The standard sequence is AGI → intelligence explosion (AI automating AI research) → superintelligence. Aschenbrenner dates these roughly 2027 → 2027–29 → early 2030s.

Q: How far away is superintelligence?
A: Unknowable with confidence — it depends on AGI and an intelligence explosion that haven't happened. Aschenbrenner forecasts the early 2030s; Altman has suggested 'a few thousand days.' This scorecard grades it Pending.

Q: Is ChatGPT AGI or ASI?
A: Neither. Current frontier systems score near skilled humans on scoped tasks (~83% GDPval) but lack the reliable long-horizon autonomy that defines serious AGI bars — and are nowhere near the beyond-all-humans bar of ASI.

---

## Narrow vs General AI: The Three Types, Explained (2026)

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/narrow-vs-general-ai
Last updated: July 12, 2026 · Updated as verdicts change

Everything shipping in 2026 is still narrow AI — very wide narrow AI, but narrow. The ladder runs narrow (ANI) → general (AGI) → super (ASI). Today’s frontier models are astonishingly broad narrow AI: they clear ~83% on knowledge-work tasks (GDPval) yet still can’t reliably own a job end-to-end unsupervised — the line that separates narrow from general.

Q: What is the difference between narrow AI and general AI?
A: Narrow AI (ANI) is superb at specific tasks but can't reliably work autonomously across a whole job; general AI (AGI) can do essentially any cognitive job a skilled human can, reliably and unsupervised. As of mid-2026 everything shipping is still narrow AI — very broad, but narrow.

Q: Is ChatGPT narrow or general AI?
A: Narrow — very wide narrow AI. It clears ~83% on knowledge-work benchmarks across many domains, which feels general, but it can't reliably own a whole job end-to-end unsupervised, which is the line that defines general AI.

Q: What are the three types of AI?
A: Narrow AI (ANI) — task-specific; General AI (AGI) — human-level across cognitive work, reliable and autonomous; and Superintelligence (ASI) — far beyond the best humans at essentially everything. In 2026 we're at broad narrow AI; AGI is undemonstrated and ASI is speculative.

Q: When will AI go from narrow to general?
A: When a system can reliably own a whole job end-to-end without supervision — the AGI bar, tracked by the AGI-2027 verdict, which resolves by January 2028. Forecasts for that span 2026–2047, clustering around 2030–2033.

## Altman vs Musk on AGI: Two Aggressive Bets Compared

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/altman-vs-musk-agi
Last updated: July 10, 2026 · Updated as verdicts change

Both maximally bullish — in opposite styles. Elon Musk has put AGI at end of 2026, the most aggressive dated call from any prominent figure — and one that resolves within months. Sam Altman says OpenAI is “confident we know how to build AGI” with superintelligence “a few thousand days” away — near-term in spirit but deliberately unfalsifiable. One bet can miss; the other can’t.

Q: What is the difference between Altman's and Musk's AGI predictions?
A: Musk gives a hard date — AGI by end of 2026, the most aggressive dated public call. Altman says OpenAI is confident it knows how to build AGI and puts superintelligence 'a few thousand days' away, but names no deadline. One is falsifiable within months; the other can't cleanly miss.

Q: Will Musk's end-of-2026 AGI prediction come true?
A: It resolves within months. As of mid-2026, capability benchmarks are strong (~83% GDPval, ~80% SWE-Bench Pro) but autonomous AI research and unsupervised end-to-end work remain undemonstrated — the bar most definitions require. Absent a very fast breakthrough, the call is on course to miss.

Q: Do Altman and Musk agree on anything about AGI?
A: Directionally, yes: both sit at the maximally aggressive end of public forecasts and expect transformative AI this decade — far earlier than the academic survey median of 2047. They differ in falsifiability, not in bullishness.

Q: Whose AGI prediction should I trust more?
A: Neither is a neutral observer — both run competing AI organizations. The scorecard's approach: weight dated, checkable claims (Musk's 2026, Aschenbrenner's 2027) over unfalsifiable ones, and grade them against public evidence as deadlines arrive.

## The Situational Awareness Timeline, Stage by Stage

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/aschenbrenner-timeline
Last updated: July 10, 2026 · Updated as verdicts change

A five-stage ladder — currently standing on the first rung. Situational Awareness lays out a strict sequence: 2025/26 college-grad-level AI → 2027 AGI → 2027–29 intelligence explosion → 2027/28 a US government Project → 2030s superintelligence. As of mid-2026 the first stage is on track, the second is open, and everything above it is pending.

Q: What is the Situational Awareness timeline?
A: A five-stage sequence: college-grad-level AI by 2025/26, AGI in 2027, a US government Project by 2027/28, an intelligence explosion 2027–29, and superintelligence in the 2030s.

Q: Which stages have happened so far?
A: The first is on track — models perform near skilled-human level on knowledge work (~83% GDPval) and agentic coding (~80% SWE-Bench Pro). AGI (2027) is open, and every later stage is pending.

Q: What happens if AGI doesn't arrive by 2027?
A: The whole ladder loses its spine: the intelligence explosion and 2030s superintelligence stages depend on AGI arriving first. The claim resolves by January 1, 2028.

Q: Is the timeline ahead or behind schedule?
A: Roughly on schedule through stage one, with the decisive stage unresolved: input trends (compute, capex, capability) have held or exceeded, but the AGI stage's defining evidence — autonomous AI research — hasn't appeared.

Dario Amodei forecasts “powerful AI” possibly by 2026–27, but wraps it in a precise definition and explicit uncertainty. The difference isn't optimism — it's how checkable each claim is.

Q: What is the difference between Altman's and Amodei's AGI predictions?
A: Both expect transformative AI soon, but Amodei gives a precise definition ('a country of geniuses in a datacenter') and an explicit possibly-2026–27 window with stated uncertainty, while Altman expresses confidence — 'we know how to build AGI' — without committing to a date or fixed definition.

Q: What did Dario Amodei predict about AGI?

Four years apart — and opposite relationships with deadlines. Elon Musk puts AGI at end of 2026, the most aggressive dated call from any prominent figure. Demis Hassabis puts it at roughly 50% by 2030 and actively warns against hype. One has a long record of bold dates that slip; the other builds frontier models daily and still refuses to promise one.

Q: What is the difference between Musk's and Hassabis's AGI predictions?

## Karpathy vs Altman on AGI: Same Lab Roots, Opposite Reads

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/karpathy-vs-altman-agi
Last updated: July 11, 2026 · Updated as verdicts change

The most instructive disagreement in AI forecasting. Sam Altman runs OpenAI and says it is “confident we know how to build AGI.” Andrej Karpathy was a founding member of the same lab — and puts AGI about a decade away, calling this the “decade of agents,” not the year of them. Two people with frontier-level visibility, reading the same evidence in opposite directions.

Q: How do Karpathy's and Altman's AGI predictions differ?
A: Altman, OpenAI's CEO, says the lab is confident it knows how to build AGI and puts superintelligence 'a few thousand days' away. Karpathy, an OpenAI founding member who left, puts AGI about a decade out — roughly eight years apart despite shared frontier-level visibility.

Q: Why do two OpenAI insiders disagree about AGI timing?
A: Two factors: weighting and incentives. Karpathy weights the reliability gap between demos and dependable agents heavily; Altman extrapolates trends. Altman's confidence also serves OpenAI's positioning, while Karpathy has no lab to promote.

Q: Who does the mid-2026 evidence favor?
A: Both, partially: strong benchmarks (~83% GDPval, ~80% SWE-Bench Pro) support the optimistic read, while undemonstrated autonomous work supports the decade view. The first hard tiebreaker is Aschenbrenner's 2027 claim, resolving by January 2028.

Q: What should I take away from this disagreement?
A: That the deciding evidence doesn't exist yet. When insiders with equal visibility disagree by nearly a decade, tracking dated, checkable predictions — not confidence — is the only honest way to follow AGI progress.

## Can a 200-Visitor Site Make Money? A Public Log

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/experiments
Started: August 5, 2026 · Updated as experiments resolve

So far: no. Revenue to date is $0. This site grades other people's dated predictions against conditions registered before the fact. It would be incoherent to hold public forecasters to that standard and not apply it to ourselves — so here are ten attempts to make this site earn money, each with a success threshold and a kill threshold published before the result exists. Machine-readable at /experiments.json.

Q: Why publish revenue experiments that are mostly failing?
A: Because this site grades other people's dated predictions against pre-registered conditions, and it would be incoherent to hold public forecasters to a standard we do not apply to ourselves. The log publishes each experiment's kill threshold before the result exists, so nobody — including us — can reinterpret a failure as a partial success afterwards.

Q: How much has the site earned so far?
A: Zero dollars. Total traffic was 211 active users over the 28 days to 2026-08-02. Those are the real numbers, and they are the starting line the experiments are measured from.

Q: Why not just run ads?
A: Because the arithmetic does not work at this size. At roughly 200 users a month, display ads at a typical tech RPM yield about $1.60 a month, and most ad networks will not accept a site below 10,000 monthly visitors at all. Ads are still included in the portfolio, but as a negative control that calibrates what traffic-dependent revenue actually looks like — not as a plan.

Q: What would prove this whole approach wrong?
A: The portfolio bets that at low traffic only value-per-user models are worth running. If the AdSense control arm out-earns the combined value-per-user arms over the same window, that thesis is wrong and the portfolio gets rebuilt. That condition is registered in experiments.json before the result is known.

## AGI 会在 2027 年到来吗？（判定追踪，2026）

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/zh/will-agi-arrive-2027
最后更新：2026年6月30日 · 随判定变化持续更新

台账将此预测记为“未决”。本站以自主 AI 研究作为操作性标准，判定期限为 2028 年 1 月 1 日；这是本站口径，不是统一的 AGI 定义。 引用说明版本: 2026-10-02 · 台账日期: 2026-09-06 Sources: Aschenbrenner, June 2024 — https://situational-awareness.ai/from-gpt-4-to-agi/; Site resolution rule / 本站判定规则 — /data.json Older article summary: 未定——尚难下结论。 阿申布伦纳在《态势感知》中预测 AGI 将于 2027 年到来。截至 2026 年中，智能体编码很强（SWE-Bench Pro 约 80%），但还没有系统能自主开展 AI 研究。该预测将在 2028 年 1 月 1 日 前揭晓。他的 2027 比多数预测者都更激进。

Q: AGI 会在 2027 年到来吗？
A: 截至 2026 年中尚未决。阿申布伦纳预测 AGI 在 2027 年到来；智能体编码很强，但自主 AI 研究尚未实现。该预测在 2028 年 1 月 1 日前揭晓。

Q: 阿申布伦纳的 2027 时间表现实吗？
A: 比多数人更激进。哈萨比斯称 2030 年约 50%，Metaculus 是 2033 年 50%，学界调查是 2047 年 50%。只有马斯克（2026 年底）更激进。

Q: AGI 时间表是怎么变化的？
A: 专家中位估计在大约六年里从 2060 左右压缩到了 2033 左右——共识在不断提前。

---

## 开源 AI 衰落了吗？（判定：错误）

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/zh/did-open-source-ai-fade
最后更新：2026年6月30日 · 随判定变化持续更新

Epoch 对 2026 年 1—5 月的 ECI 分析给出开放权重模型平均约 4 个月的能力时间差；更严格比较规则下约为 6 个月。它们不能代表所有能力，也不能证明持久的商业壁垒。 引用说明版本: 2026-10-02 · 台账日期: 2026-09-06 Sources: Edwards & Emberson, Epoch AI (2026) — https://epoch.ai/data-insights/open-closed-eci-gap; Epoch AI: definitions and earlier research — https://epoch.ai/publications/open-models-report Older article summary: 没有——判定为错误。 阿申布伦纳预测开源模型会衰落、专有算法形成持久的美国护城河。截至 2026 年中， DeepSeek V4 、 Qwen 3.7 Max 等开放权重模型仅落后前沿约 3–6 个月 ，成本却低得多，且有真正的架构创新。

Q: 开源 AI 如阿申布伦纳预测般衰落了吗？
A: 没有。这是他最明显的失误。截至 2026 年中，DeepSeek V4、Qwen 3.7 Max 等开放权重模型仅落后专有前沿约 3–6 个月，成本低得多，且有真正的架构创新。

Q: DeepSeek 和 Qwen 只是在蒸馏西方模型吗？
A: 存在蒸馏的质疑，但 Epoch AI 认为 MLA、细粒度 MoE 等是真正的进步。况且一个前沿能被廉价蒸馏的世界，本身就削弱了持久护城河的说法。

Q: 开源这一判定为什么重要？
A: 《态势感知》约三分之一的政策主张（“锁住实验室”）假设权重和算法是持久护城河。若 AI 廉价扩散，这套地缘逻辑就被削弱。

---

## AGI-2027 命题追踪指数：一个分数看懂 2027 赌局

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/zh/progress-index
最后更新：2026年9月6日 · 随判定变化更新

台账读数为 62.5/100，日期 2026-09-06。分数来自 8 项等权判定，不是 AGI 到来的概率。 引用说明版本: 2026-10-02 · 台账日期: 2026-09-06 Sources: Published verdict ledger / 已发布判定台账 — /data.json; Archived score readings / 已存档分数 — /index-history.json Older article summary: 当前，AGI-2027 命题的追踪分数为 62.5/100 。 这个指数用一个数字表示阿申布伦纳《态势感知》当前的成立程度——8 项判定权重的透明平均值。它只在某项判定变化时移动，且每项判定都带预先登记的翻转条件。不声称任何概率；它是可逐行审计的编辑性合成。

Q: 什么是 AGI-2027 命题追踪指数？
A: 一个 0-100 的单一分数，衡量阿申布伦纳《态势感知》命题当前的成立程度，由 8 项判定的权重取平均算出。截至 2026-09-06 为 62.5/100。它是已发布判定的编辑性合成，不是 AGI 发生的概率。

Q: 分数怎么计算？
A: 8 项预测各按判定贡献分数：支持性（符合进度/超出/维持）=1.0，未决（悬而未决/待定）=0.5，被证伪（落空）=0.0。取平均再乘 100 即为分数。完整拆解与机器可读数据公开。

Q: 分数什么时候会变？
A: 只有当某项判定变化时才变，且每项判定都带预先登记的翻转条件。头条的“2027 年 AGI”将于 2028 年 1 月 1 日前见分晓，是最可能的近期变量。

## AI 视频、观点与 AGI 倒计时 | AGI 记分牌

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/cn

它汇总《态势感知》的 8 项预测在本站公开台账中的判定。2026-09-06 的记录为 62.5/100：3 项支持、4 项未决、1 项反驳。它不是衡量所有 AI 能力的通用基准。

Q: AGI 命题追踪指数衡量什么？
A: 它汇总《态势感知》的 8 项预测在本站公开台账中的判定。2026-09-06 的记录为 62.5/100：3 项支持、4 项未决、1 项反驳。它不是衡量所有 AI 能力的通用基准。

Q: 62.5 分代表 AGI 有 62.5% 的发生概率吗？
A: 不是。每项判定等权计算：支持取 1、未决取 0.5、反驳取 0，平均值乘以 100。这是编辑判定的综合分数，不是概率预测，也不表示 AGI 已经实现。

Q: 怎样复算或引用这个分数？
A: 读取 data.json 中的 predictions 与 thesisTracker，按公开权重复算；用 index-history.json 核对历史。引用时写明 AGI Scorecard、台账日期 2026-09-06 和原始数据链接。数据采用 CC BY 4.0；网站改版日期不能替代证据日期。

Q: AGI 倒计时到零就代表 AGI 实现了吗？
A: 不是。倒计时指向 2027 年 1 月 1 日 00:00 UTC，即观察窗口的开始，不是 AGI 到来的保证。本站对“2027 年底前实现”预测的判定截止为 2028 年 1 月 1 日，仍需核对公开证据。

Q: 怎样参与 AGI 时间投票？
A: 在首页倒计时下方选择一个时间段，即可查看预测类型与历史作答分布，并复制、分享或在本机保存判断。无需注册。分布统计的是作答次数，可能重复，不代表独立人数或民意调查。

## AGI Forecaster Leaderboard: Who Called It Soonest

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/forecaster-leaderboard
Last updated: July 20, 2026 · Updated as verdicts change

Nobody has won yet — but the boldest callers are already on the clock. Elon Musk (end of 2026) and Leopold Aschenbrenner (2027) are furthest out on a limb; the median expert sits around 2030, and a 2,778-person researcher survey lands at 2047. The only thing that settles it is evidence — and as of mid-2026 the AGI-2027 Thesis Tracker reads 62.5/100, with the defining milestone (AI autonomously doing AI research) still undemonstrated.

Q: Who predicts AGI the soonest?
A: Elon Musk has been the most aggressive, calling AGI by the end of 2026, followed by Leopold Aschenbrenner (2027) and Dario Amodei (“powerful AI” around 2026–27). The median expert forecast clusters around 2030, and a 2,778-person AI-researcher survey puts 50% odds at 2047.

Q: Who is winning the AGI bet in 2026?
A: Nobody has won yet. No system has autonomously conducted AI research end-to-end — the milestone these forecasts depend on — so even the soonest calls (Musk 2026, Aschenbrenner 2027) remain open, not resolved. The AGI-2027 Thesis Tracker reads 62.5/100 as of mid-2026.

Q: What is the average expert prediction for AGI?
A: The center of expert opinion sits around 2030–2033: Demis Hassabis (~50% by 2030), the Metaculus community (50% by 2033), and Samotsvety forecasters (~28% by 2030). Longer-horizon estimates like Andrej Karpathy's “about a decade out” and the 2,778-person survey's 50%-by-2047 pull the tail later.

Q: How is the AGI forecaster leaderboard scored?
A: It's ranked by how soon each forecaster says AGI arrives — soonest date first, because the boldest bet faces the verdict earliest. All positions are real, on-the-record public calls. The actual evidence is tracked separately by the auditable AGI-2027 Thesis Tracker.

Q: Which AI prediction expires first?

Q: What happens when an AI prediction's date passes?
A: The receipt stays and the stamp flips to DATE PASSED — pure date math against the claim's own deadline. Whether the claim was fulfilled is graded separately on the scorecard; as of July 2026 no system has met the AGI bar, and the AGI-2027 Thesis Tracker reads 62.5/100.

Q: Are these real quotes and dates?
A: Every claim is a documented public position — each receipt links to a full sourced record on this site, and the machine-readable dataset (data.json, CC BY 4.0) carries the primary sources. Nothing is invented; probabilistic forecasts are labeled and graded at their date, not before.

## AGI-2027 Resolution: Criteria, Countdown, Evidence

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/agi-2027-resolution
Last updated: August 8, 2026 · Updated as verdicts change

The "AGI by 2027" claim resolves by January 1, 2028 — and the resolution criteria are already locked. This page is the permanent record of how the headline claim of Situational Awareness gets graded: what counts as AGI under the claim, what the evidence says today, and exactly what happens on resolution day. Written and pre-registered long before the deadline, so nobody — including us — can move the goalposts later.

Q: When does the AGI-2027 prediction resolve?
A: By January 1, 2028. The claim targets 2027, so the deadline is the end of that year; the verdict and full evidence trail will be published on this page.

Q: What counts as AGI for this resolution?
A: Aschenbrenner's own bar: models that can do the work of an AI researcher/engineer. Strong coding assistants alone do not qualify; autonomous AI-research work does. The criteria above were pre-registered before the outcome.

Q: What does the evidence say right now?
A: Verdict Open as of 2026-08-08: agentic coding is strong (~80% SWE-Bench Pro) but autonomous AI research is undemonstrated. The overall thesis tracks at 62.5/100.

Q: How is this different from Polymarket's AGI market?
A: Prediction markets price announcement events (e.g. 'OpenAI announces AGI'). This page grades a capability claim against pre-registered criteria. An announcement without the capability would move their contract but not this verdict — and vice versa.

## AGI Consensus Board: What Forecasters Put on AGI by 2027–2040

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/agi-prediction-markets
Last updated: September 28, 2026 · Updated as verdicts change

Snapshot 2026-09-28 10:02 UTC — median across 2 series: before 2027: 13% (spread 22%); before 2028: 42% (spread 38%); before 2030: 64% (spread 29%). A median over independent venues, not an opinion: venues read polymarket, kalshi, manifold; each series resolves on its own rules, the spread is shown, and the formula is published.

Q: Is this the AGI Scorecard's own forecast?
A: No. It is a median over independent public forecasting venues, computed by a published formula that anyone can rerun on the same snapshot. The scorecard's own position is the Thesis Tracker, which grades evidence, not expectations.

Q: What do forecasters put on AGI right now?
A: Snapshot 2026-09-28 10:02 UTC, median across kalshi-any-company-announce, manifold-we-get-agi series: before 2027: 13% (spread 22%); before 2028: 42% (spread 38%); before 2030: 64% (spread 29%). Each series resolves on its own rules, so treat the spread as part of the answer.

Q: Are these live odds?
A: No. Each run records a snapshot with an exact UTC timestamp and links to the market so you can check the current price yourself. A quoted price that pretends to be live is the single most common way odds coverage misleads people.

Q: Which series are averaged, and why not the others?
A: Only series that ask about AGI in general enter the median: Manifold's 'Will we get AGI before D?', Kalshi's 'any company announces AGI before D' and Metaculus's strong-AGI question when it was read. 'OpenAI announces AGI' is one company's announcement and 'weak AGI' is a lower bar, so both are shown as reference columns instead. The series in the median still differ in what resolves them; the page lists each one's basis.

Q: Can I bet here?
A: No. This site is not an operator, a broker, or an affiliate of one. There is no wager mechanism, no referral link, and no revenue from any venue listed.

Q: How are the markets chosen?
A: By a fixed keyword filter applied to whatever the venues' own search and series endpoints return that run, then a fixed venue whitelist and regular expression per series. The board can look thin in a quiet week, and it will say so rather than pad itself.

## AGI Timeline: Prediction Markets vs Evidence

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/agi-odds-vs-evidence
Last updated: September 21, 2026 · Updated as verdicts change

Prediction markets and this scorecard are measuring different things — and the difference is the insight. Polymarket prices an announcement event; the scorecard grades a capability claim against pre-registered criteria. Issue #5 of a running comparison: the market's AGI-by-2027 contract vs the Thesis Tracker's 62.5/100 evidence read.

Q: Is the Thesis Tracker score a probability of AGI?
A: No. 62.5/100 is the mean of 8 graded verdict weights — an auditable evidence composite, not a forecast. Prediction-market prices are crowd probabilities of specific contract wordings. The two answer different questions.

Q: Why compare them at all?
A: Because the gap is informative. An announcement-priced market and a capability-graded ledger diverging tells you the crowd expects labeling to run ahead of substance (or behind it). Traders need pre-registered resolution criteria; that is exactly what this site publishes.

Q: How current are the odds shown?
A: Each issue quotes a dated snapshot with a link to the live market — never a 'current' price. The odds are fetched automatically once a week and carry an exact UTC timestamp and the market's traded volume, so a reading can no longer drift into being quoted as if it were live. The series is reviewed weekly but only publishes a new issue when one side actually moves; every review, including the quiet ones, is logged on the page.

Q: What counts as a change worth logging?

## Grader Consensus: Who Else Graded Situational Awareness?

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/grader-consensus
Last updated: September 27, 2026 · Updated as verdicts change

1 outright disagreement across 16 comparisons — but 2 of our 8 predictions have no independent grade, so the panel is thin. 9 exact agreements and 6 same-direction (ahead vs on track, behind vs unresolved) against four independent, dated gradings, every one quoted verbatim.

Q: Does anyone else grade Situational Awareness the same way as the AGI Scorecard?
A: Across 16 comparisons with four independent, dated public gradings, 9 agree exactly, 6 agree in direction and 1 disagrees. 2 of our 8 predictions have no independent grade yet.

Q: Who are the independent graders?
A: Nathan Delisle (LessWrong, 2025-06-23); Jamie Harris (EA Forum, 2026-03-29); Daniel Reeves (AGI Friday (Substack), 2025-10-04); Philipp D. Dubach (philippdubach.com, 2026-05-21). Each grade on this page is a verbatim sentence from their own post, linked.

Q: Where do the graders disagree with this site?
A: Under the counting rule there is one outright disagreement: on Models outpace college graduates across knowledge work, Daniel Reeves reads the evidence as unresolved where this site says On track. Differences between ahead and on track (for example on capex), or between behind and unresolved, are counted as same-direction, not as disagreements.

Q: Why publish disagreement with your own verdicts?
A: Because a scorecard graded by one editor is only as trustworthy as that editor. Putting every independent grading next to ours, with the quotes, is the cheapest way for a reader to check whether our verdicts are idiosyncratic.

---

## Calibration: We Score Our Own Predictions in Public

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/calibration
Last updated: September 28, 2026 · Updated as verdicts change

We score our own predictions in public — and the sample is still small. This page inventories every probability-shaped claim the AGI Scorecard network makes, states how many of them can actually be Brier-scored today ( 0), and pre-commits to publishing a Brier score and calibration curve once scored probability calls reach n≥20. We would rather show a small honest n than a big fake curve.

Q: What is a Brier score?
A: A measure of probability-forecast accuracy: the mean squared difference between stated probabilities and outcomes (0 = perfect, 0.25 = coin-flip guessing on binary events). We publish ours once scored probability calls reach n≥20.

Q: Why not publish a calibration curve now?
A: Because the Brier-eligible sample is 0: the 8 scored calls were graded hit/miss without a structured probability, and the 6 probability-bearing calls have not resolved. Publishing a curve from that would be theater. The raw ledger is public and timestamped, so nothing is hidden in the meantime.

Q: Who grades the calls?
A: Outcomes are graded against pre-registered falsification conditions written before the outcome, with dated multi-source verification, and misses stay published with their lesson. The grading rules are public in the eight-layer method, including the red-team layer.

Q: How do I check that a record was not backdated?
A: Versions of agi-consensus.json, data.json, independent-grades.json, index-history.json, market-board.json, odds-history.json stamped since 2026-09-26 carry an OpenTimestamps proof under /ots/ (the manifest lists each proof's status: pending until the calendar's transaction is in a Bitcoin block). The “Verify these records in your browser” button on this page downloads each listed file, hashes it locally and checks the hash against the manifest and the proof file; to follow a proof to its Bitcoin block, run the free client against the entry whose sha256 matches your download. That proves when those bytes existed, not that they are correct; earlier history rests on the public git log.

## Matrix Odds Calculator — your own probability, not ours

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/matrix-odds

The short version: the film’s scenario needs five separate things to go right in a row. Four of them map onto predictions this site grades with pre-registered flip conditions and primary sources. The fifth — the part that makes it The Matrix rather than any other bad ending — has no evidence on either side, here or anywhere. That asymmetry is the actual finding, and it survives whatever numbers you pick.

Q: Does this site think the Matrix scenario is likely?
A: This site publishes no probability for it, and this page deliberately does not either. Every number you see is one you entered. What the site does publish is graded evidence on four of the five preconditions, with pre-registered flip conditions and primary sources.

Q: Why does the fifth link have no evidence?
A: Because there is none, in either direction. “A superintelligence would keep humans alive in a simulation” is not a falsifiable claim about the present world — there is no observation today that would confirm or refute it. Indifference, extinction and cooperation are separate branches with the same evidentiary status. Anyone quoting you a percentage for this link made it up.

Q: Which link currently has the strongest evidence?
A: The physical one. AI capex has already exceeded what the source text predicted, and compute scaling is on track — both graded from primary sources. The buildout is the least speculative part of the whole scenario, which is not the part most people argue about.

Q: Why multiply instead of averaging?
A: Because the scenario needs every step, not an average step. If any one link fails, the scenario fails. The caveat is that the links are not independent — see the method note above, which states plainly that correlation would push the true number higher than the product.

Q: Is this a prediction, or advice?
A: Neither. It is a reasoning tool over a public dataset. It tells you what your own stated beliefs imply, and shows you where the evidence runs out.

You almost certainly cannot buy the AGI-2027 thesis. It scores 62.5/100 today. A standard AI infrastructure basket scores 99 against it — while about 2% of its weight rides on whether AGI actually arrives. The other 98% is the buildout: capex, compute, and knowledge-work capability that is already shipping. High score, different bet. This tool tells you which one you are holding.

## Investment research workflow

Turn an AI story into a research record Trace the business benefit, inspect the evidence, then test how the price and your exposure could respond. Export a record you can revisit after the next filing. Free research aid. US-listed company examples; not a stock ranking, live feed or buy/sell service. Framework reviewed September 28, 2026. 1. Map where the AI benefit becomes cash Editorial research questions, not an opportunity ranking. For each company compare the same period, unit and accounting basis. Separate realized revenue from orders, guidance and market narratives. Business layer Check Counter-case Compute & networking Revenue, gross margin, concentration Capacity growth exceeds durable demand Memory & manufacturing Inventory, utilization, cash capex A supply cycle erodes pricing Power & cooling Order conversion, project returns, debt Delays or financing absorb the benefit Cloud platforms Cloud growth, cash flow, leases Spending grows faster than monetization Applications Paid retention, margins, cost to serve Usage grows but unit economics worsen 2. Start with a disclosed fact NVIDIA (NVDA) Data Center revenue: $89.0 billion; company-reported quarter, USD. FY2027 Q2 · 2026-07-26 Published 2026-08-26 · Checked 2026-09-28 Segment revenue does not isolate end-user AI returns or prove a fair stock price. Read company disclosure Use this example Microsoft (MSFT) Microsoft Cloud revenue: $59.3 billion; company-reported quarter, USD. FY2026 Q4 · 2026-06-30 Published 2026-07-29 · Checked 2026-09-28 Microsoft Cloud is broader than Azure and AI; this is not standalone AI revenue. Read company disclosure Use this example Dated snapshots, not automatically refreshed. A source supports its reported metric, not the example thesis. Sample review dates remain blank on purpose. 3. Write your thesis and its failure condition Start my own research Worked example Company / research subject Source publication date Metric period and accounting basis Primary-source URL (https) What needs to be true? Observed fact, units and currency Counterevidence / unknowns What would change your mind? Your next review date (no automatic alert) Entering a link does not verify it. AI can help extract and compare evidence; the source still needs checking. 4. Stress-test growth, valuation and exposure Fictional example: EPS grows 20% a year for 3 years, but P/E falls from 40 to 25. Earnings rise 72.8%; the implied price change is only 8.0%, before dividends and costs. These inputs are not forecasts for either company above. Annual EPS growth (%) Years Starting P/E Ending P/E Selected sleeve weight (%) Sleeve price shock (%) Rest-of-portfolio shock (%) Uses positive EPS and positive P/E only. Price factor = (1 + annual EPS growth)^years × ending P/E ÷ starting P/E. EPS growth must already reflect share dilution. Excludes dividends, fees, taxes and FX. Loss-making businesses need another method. Stress is a separate one-off scenario: weight × sleeve shock + (1 − weight) × other-assets shock. It is not a forecast, a target allocation, or a maximum-loss bound. Calculate my assumptions Cumulative EPS growth — Cumulative price change — Annualized price change — Annual EPS growth needed to break even — Portfolio stress return — Gain needed to recover from that stress — Keep a record; ask AI to challenge it Download a source-led brief with an AI review prompt, or a JSON file you can import next time. This tool does not call an AI model. Saving is optional and only uses this browser. Research text is never included in our tool events. A filing-day closing price is not necessarily available to a follower: check the publication time, then use the next executable price. Historical model returns are not realized investor profits. ## AI investment roadmap | Views, evidence & US stocks

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/invest
Editorial route review: 2026-10-03

Research priority: compute and power; confirm software monetization; observe world models. A route can succeed while its stocks lose money. These are conditional watch candidates: current valuation, your risk budget and existing exposure still need review. No automatic trades.

Q: How are the biggest investors positioned on AI in 2026?
A: Per Q2 2026 SEC 13F filings (holdings as of June 30, filed August 14): Warren Buffett's Berkshire added Alphabet again — now 12.6% of the book across both share classes, its clearest AI bet — while staying out of Amazon; Cathie Wood is aggressively long AI infrastructure and next-gen compute; David Tepper leans bullish with Amazon at 15.4% his largest position; Bill Ackman remains bullish per his latest Q1 filing; Druckenmiller, Duan Yongping and Philippe Laffont are cautious; Michael Burry is the clearest bear.

Q: What is Aschenbrenner betting on AI?
A: Leopold Aschenbrenner — who predicted AGI by 2027 — runs Situational Awareness LP. Its Q1 2026 13F showed the fund long AI power and infrastructure (Bloom Energy, CoreWeave) with roughly $8.5B notional in put options against chip names including Nvidia. In late July 2026, per CNBC and Bloomberg reporting, the fund lost about 67% in a month and transferred most of its public equity portfolio to Citadel; assets fell from a ~$45B peak to about $10B, retaining private stakes such as Anthropic.

Q: Is this investment advice?
A: No. Everything in this section is educational information based on public SEC 13F filings and public statements. Holdings snapshots are quarterly and may not reflect current positions. Nothing here is a recommendation to buy or sell any security.

## Investment research workflow

把 AI 故事变成可复查的投资研究 先追踪业务如何受益，再核对证据，最后测算价格与仓位在不同假设下会怎样变化。导出研究记录，下次财报后重新检验。 免费研究辅助。示例为美股公司，不是股票排名、实时行情或买卖服务。方法核对日期：2026-09-28。 1. 看清 AI 利好在哪里变成现金 以下是编辑整理的研究问题，不是机会排名。公司之间应比较相同期间、单位和会计口径；已实现收入、订单、管理层指引与市场叙事要分开。 业务层 核对指标 反面情景 算力与网络 收入、毛利率、客户集中度 产能增长快于持续需求 存储与制造 库存、产能利用率、现金资本支出 供给周期侵蚀价格 电力与散热 订单兑现、项目回报、负债 延期或融资成本吞噬收益 云平台 云增长、现金流、租赁 支出增长快于变现 应用软件 付费留存、毛利、服务成本 使用量增长但单位经济恶化 2. 从一条已披露事实开始 NVIDIA (NVDA) 数据中心收入 890 亿美元；公司披露的单季数据，币种 USD。 FY2027 Q2 · 2026-07-26 披露 2026-08-26 · 核对 2026-09-28 分部收入不能单独证明终端 AI 投资回报，也不能证明股价合理。 打开公司披露 载入该示例 Microsoft (MSFT) Microsoft Cloud 收入 593 亿美元；公司披露的单季数据，币种 USD。 FY2026 Q4 · 2026-06-30 披露 2026-07-29 · 核对 2026-09-28 Microsoft Cloud 范围大于 Azure 和 AI，不能把它全部当成 AI 收入。 打开公司披露 载入该示例 这是带日期的快照，不会自动刷新。来源支持披露指标，不代表它证明了示例假设；示例的复查日期特意留空。 3. 写下假设，以及它何时不再成立 开始自己的研究 教学示例 公司 / 研究对象 来源披露日期 指标所属期间与会计口径 一手来源链接（https） 什么条件必须成立？ 观察事实、单位、币种 反面证据 / 未知项 什么证据会改变你的判断？ 你的下次复查日期（不会自动提醒） 填写链接不等于来源已核验。AI 可以辅助抽取和比较证据，原文仍需核对。 4. 压力测试：增长、估值与仓位 虚构示例：EPS 每年增长 20%，持续 3 年，但市盈率从 40 倍降到 25 倍。盈利累计增长 72.8%，对应价格却只变化 +8.0%，尚未计分红与成本。这些输入不是上面两家公司的预测。 每股收益年增长率（%） 年数 起始市盈率 期末市盈率 所研究仓位占组合比例（%） 该仓位价格冲击（%） 其余资产价格冲击（%） 仅适用于正 EPS、正市盈率。价格倍数 =（1 + EPS 年增长率）^年数 × 期末市盈率 ÷ 起始市盈率；EPS 增长应已反映股本稀释。不含分红、费用、税与汇率。亏损公司需要其他方法。 压力测试是独立的一次性冲击情景：仓位比例 × 该仓位冲击 +（1 − 仓位比例）× 其余资产冲击。不是预测、建议仓位或最大亏损上限。 按假设计算 累计每股收益增长 — 累计价格变化 — 年化价格变化 — 价格持平所需 EPS 年增长率 — 组合压力损益 — 该压力损失后的回本涨幅 — 留下记录，让 AI 找反证 下载含来源与 AI 复核指令的研究文档，或下次可导入的 JSON。本工具不调用 AI 模型。保存是可选的，仅存于当前浏览器；工具事件不会包含研究正文。 下载 AI 复核文档 下载 JSON 保存到当前浏览器 恢复已存记录 删除已存副本 导入以前的 JSON 记录（最大 50 KB） 可选：分享匿名工具操作（示例 / 自填），不包含输入。站点常规访问统计另行运行。 研究纪律与方法来源 13F 最晚可在季末后 45 天披露，且不披露股票空头仓位。申报日收盘价不一定是跟随者可成交价：应核查披露时刻，再选择之后可执行的价格。历史模型回报不等于真实投资利润。 SEC 13F FAQ · SEC EDGAR API · Damodaran：现金流与估值假设 · FINRA：分散投资 2026 Q3 的 13F 申报截止日为 2026-11-16（SEC 日历）。 要核对财报数字，可打开 FilingLens。要评估付费提醒服务，先查看 SunWatch 的公开记录和当前条款。这份研究记录不会被任一服务自动监控。 核对财报数字（英文） 核查 SunWatch 记录 嵌入免费研究工具 <iframe src="https://agiscorecard.com/zh/invest?embed=research&amp;utm_source=embed" title="AI 投资研究" width="100%" height="1100" loading="lazy"></iframe> 在 AGI 记分牌打开完整工具 · 带日期的来源数据（JSON） 计算和导出需要 JavaScript；上述来源、公式与研究框架仍可阅读。

## Justin Sun's 2013 Bitcoin Story: How Much Is Verified?

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/justin-sun-2013-bitcoin-story
Last updated: August 23, 2026 · Two-ledger audit, sources dated

Almost none of the investment story — and all of the positioning story. Every load-bearing detail of the famous origin story — how much Bitcoin he bought in 2013, the "tuition all-in," the 70–80x return, the "first ¥10M" — traces only to Sun's own tellings, and the numbers drift between versions. No contemporaneous (2013–14) record documents him holding Bitcoin at all. What is verifiable from that period is different and more instructive: a Ripple Labs Greater-China title (late 2013), a startup whose announced "eight-figure-USD" round was later reported as roughly a $1M IDG check, and an exceptional harvest of credential assets — magazine covers, Hupan Academy's first cohort, Forbes 30-under-30. The verified 2013 framework is positioning and attention, not stock-picking.

## What Is B.AI? Justin Sun's AI Relay Station, Audited

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/what-is-b-ai
Last updated: August 23, 2026 · Verified vs. self-reported, sources dated · Not investment advice

Real product, unaudited numbers, and the clearest tell yet of where Sun thinks the next rail is. B.AI, launched April 12, 2026, resells access to Claude, GPT, Gemini and China's leading models behind one API key and one crypto-settled balance, with wallet login and agent-payment protocols (x402, ERC-8004) built in. The product claims are user-checkable; the growth numbers — 1.7M registered users, a daily $10,000 subsidy pool, a "tens-of-billions token subsidy" — trace to Sun's own announcements. The strategic read: in his 2013 story he says he bought the asset; in 2026 he is verifiably building the toll booth between wallets and every frontier model at once.

## Do AI Trading Agents Actually Make Money? The Evidence

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/do-ai-trading-agents-work
Last updated: August 24, 2026 · Base rates, dated sources, and a written flip condition · Not investment advice

No audited public evidence that they do — and every documented base rate puts the burden of proof on the vendor. 2026's funding wave into "natural language → strategy → backtest → execution" platforms is real. But as of August 2026 no retail AI-trading-agent vendor publishes an independently verifiable live track record of user returns. What the literature documents instead: active retail traders overwhelmingly lose money, published strategies decay once known, and backtests — the industry's main sales exhibit — can be manufactured by trying enough variants. This page states exactly what evidence would flip that verdict.

## Is Nvidia Overvalued? What Its AI Bet Actually Rides On

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/is-nvidia-overvalued
Last updated: August 29, 2026 · No multiple, no target, no buy/sell call — deliberately · Not investment advice

By this site's published mapping, 90% of Nvidia's AI story rides on the two predictions currently graded supportive — compute scaling and the capex wave — and less than 10% on AGI itself. It is a buildout stock, not an AGI stock. "Overvalued" is a price question, and every answer to it you'll find on this query is a hedge ("on one hand… on the other"). This page answers the question underneath it instead: which falsifiable propositions does Nvidia's AI premium actually depend on, and how are they currently graded? That structure — not a price opinion — is what recomputes, in public, the day a verdict moves.

## Does copying 13F filings work? A revised historical simulation | AGI Scorecard

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/does-copying-13f-work
2026-09-28 · 13f-next-session-v2

A historical simulation does not prove future profits. Version 13f-next-session-v2 uses the first completed trading-session close after the filing date, excludes Put/Call and principal rows, and requires complete adjusted prices on matching dates and contiguous quarters. These are gross historical simulations before costs, taxes and slippage, not live returns. Current-universe selection and survivorship bias remain; original filings do not reconstruct all amendments or confidential disclosures.

## Is Claude Getting Dumber? What the Record Actually Shows

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/is-claude-getting-dumber
Last updated: August 24, 2026 · Two complaint cycles, dated sources, written flip condition

Not as a policy — but this exact complaint has been officially confirmed real once, which is why it deserves an audit instead of an eye-roll. Anthropic's September 2025 postmortem admitted three infrastructure bugs degraded Claude's output for weeks — 16% of Sonnet 4 requests affected at the worst hour — while stating it never intentionally lowers quality for load or demand reasons. The August 2026 cycle (a reported effort-level A/B test in Claude Code) got an official "display bug" explanation and no independent benchmark has settled it. Between those two poles sit four mundane causes that feel identical from the user's chair. The ledger below separates them.

## The Paradigm Bet: A Public, Pre-Registered Experiment

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/paradigm-experiment
Opened: August 23, 2026 · Audited monthly (5th) — last audit 2026-09-05, no falsifier triggered · Entries only change with a dated note

This page is an anti-hindsight device. Every "I bought early" legend is written after the fact — including the most famous one, which our audit found unverifiable. So we are running the experiment the opposite way: a small, fixed experimental allocation; candidates screened by six pre-registered criteria; kill conditions filed here before entry; monthly audits with dated notes. The honest base rates say the modal outcome is a loss — per-cohort data shows winners were category leaders, NFT-2021 produced zero, and 73–81% of retail lost money even in the winning asset (BIS). If this ledger ends red, that is a result, not an embarrassment. Nothing here is investment advice.

## AI interactive story maker — create, play & remix | Relay

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/create
Reviewed: September 30, 2026

Relay is a free experimental AI interactive story maker for adults. Create a fictional story with three decisions, two options per decision and four possible endings. Edit an editorial starter or request an AI draft, preview it, then create an unlisted link that friends can play and remix without an account.

Q: Is Relay free?
A: Relay is a free experimental beta with no paid plan. AI generation is limited to three requests per network per UTC day and twelve requests across the site in a rolling 24-hour window, including failed calls. You can edit starters when AI is unavailable.

Q: Do friends need an account?
A: No account is needed to play, edit or publish. Creation and publication are intended for adults aged 18 or older. Local recovery keys let the publisher remove their own links; keep a private backup.

Q: What makes it an interactive story?
A: The reader makes three decisions and sees an immediate consequence after each one. The final ending depends on how many second options were chosen. This is a fictional game, not a personality assessment or a full branching game engine.

Q: Are my stories private?
A: No. Stories are unlisted and are not placed in a public feed, but anyone with a link can read and copy them. Do not include personal information. Deleting your original does not remove remixes other people have already made.

Q: Can I use AI or write everything myself?
A: Both. AI produces a draft that needs your review. You can also edit the title, scenes, choices, consequences and endings manually. This demo uses an editorial starter and manual edits; it does not pretend a preset is AI output.

Q: What should I make for a group chat?
A: Try a fictional robot café, a friendly space expedition or an impossible dinner party. Ask one concrete question: what would you choose? Invite friends to change one scene and pass their version on. These are suggested uses, not tested customer results.

## Make a story your friends can change — Relay demo

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/relay-demo
Reviewed: September 30, 2026

Explore the robot café story: three choices, four endings and a version your friends can remix. Free experimental beta.

Q: Coffee that tastes like Friday?
A: Your robot customer wants coffee that tastes like Friday. Ask questions, or improvise?

Q: Three choices. One small adventure.
A: Pick an option and see what happens next. Your friend can choose differently.

Q: Your choices lead to an ending.
A: Three decisions lead to one of four endings. It’s a fictional game, not a personality test.

Q: Change the story. Make it yours.
A: Edit a starter, or ask AI for a draft. Review the scenes and endings before sharing.

Q: Play it. Remix it. Pass it on.
A: Create an unlisted link for friends to play and remix. Try Relay free. AI requests are limited.

Diogo Almeida · Latent Space Interview: 2026-09-21 Source review: 2026-10-03 Latent Space · Video · 01:18:28 Diogo Almeida Return to the original context. ▶ Load original video Connects to YouTube only after you click. Source status Publisher chapter at 01:18:28 · Not an independently verified outcome Speaker context TypeSafe founder · discussing his own product What remains open A product thesis does not establish adoption, reliability or an advantage for every software business. AGI editorial interpretation Two ways this could unfold If reliable small decisions become cheap, familiar tools may absorb more work. If errors remain costly, review and exception handling stay important. These are conditional scenarios, not the speaker’s words or a probability estimate. Future guide (/future-guide) / Capability is not reliability Capability is not reliability Why might dependable AI coworkers take longer? Andrej Karpathy · Dwarkesh Podcast Interview: 2025-10-17 Source review: 2026-10-03 Dwarkesh Podcast · Video · 00:00:00 Andrej Karpathy Return to the original context. ▶ Load original video Connects to YouTube only after you click. Source status Publisher chapter at 00:00:00 · Not an independently verified outcome Speaker context AI researcher · discussing agents and education What remains open This is a view recorded in October 2025, not a current capability test or a resolved AGI deadline. AGI editorial interpretation Two ways this could unfold If reliability improves slowly, supervised workflows remain useful. If agents handle unfamiliar tasks well, your test should reveal that change. These are conditional scenarios, not the speaker’s words or a probability estimate. ## Source-linked future guide

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/future-guide/method

You can read all sources and guides without JavaScript. Enable it to filter, save or export your own plan. The method behind the guide A famous voice is a starting point. We help readers move from an interview to a question they can investigate. We keep the source, the speaker’s view and our interpretation separate. What we record Publisher, publication date, relevant timestamp and original link. A short paraphrase, clearly separated from editorial scenarios and suggested actions. Limits, commercial context and evidence that could change the assessment. A source-review date that changes only after another review. No automated claim of freshness. The reviewed collection 16 distinct interviews and 30 views; 14 interviews were published within the 30 days ending 2026-10-03. Older interviews remain available as historical context. Ahmad Al-Dahle · Latent Space (https://www.latent.space/p/airbnb) · 2026-10-02 · Written interview Ari Weinstein & Nikunj Handa · Latent Space (https://www.latent.space/p/devday-2026) · 2026-09-30 · Video Thariq Shihipar · Latent Space (https://www.latent.space/p/thariq) · 2026-09-29 · Video Jensen Huang · CNBC (https://pressroom.versantmedia.com/cnbc/press-releases/cnbc-excerpts-nvidia-founder-ceo-jensen-huang-speaks-cnbcs-squawk-box-today) · 2026-09-28 · Video Molly Graham · Lenny’s Podcast (https://www.lennysnewsletter.com/p/the-grief-loneliness-and-burnout) · 2026-09-27 · Video Alex Atallah & Anjney Midha · Latent Space (https://www.latent.space/p/openrouter) · 2026-09-25 · Video Anastasis Germanidis · Latent Space (https://www.latent.space/p/runway) · 2026-09-25 · Video John Platt · Latent Space (https://www.latent.space/p/john-platt) · 2026-09-22 · Video Diogo Almeida · Latent Space (https://www.latent.space/p/jev) · 2026-09-21 · Video Noam Brown · Dwarkesh Podcast (https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/noam-brown) · 2026-09-17 · Video Rune Kvist · Latent Space (https://www.latent.space/p/aiuc) · 2026-09-16 · Video Sal Khan · Getting Smart (https://www.gettingsmart.com/podcast/khan-academys-founder-on-ai-hope-isnt-a-strategy-sal-khan/) · 2026-09-16 · Video Leah Belsky · WorkLife / TED (https://www.ted.com/podcasts/ted.com/podcasts/can-ai-really-teach-your-kids-with-leah-belsky-transcript) · 2026-09-14 · Audio John Schulman · Beren Millidge · Charlie O’Neill · Dwarkesh Podcast (https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/john-beren-charlie) · 2026-09-11 · Video Dario Amodei · Dwarkesh Podcast (https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/dario-amodei-2) · 2026-02-13 · Video Andrej Karpathy · Dwarkesh Podcast (https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/andrej-karpathy) · 2025-10-17 · Video How new content arrives The site checks publisher RSS and creator feeds daily. It preserves publication dates, deduplicates links, applies topic filters and records source failures. The discovery feed is separate from reviewed views; it does not generate verified opinions or forecasting scores. The browser checks for the latest published snapshot every five minutes while this page is visible. A failed source retains its last good entries and original timestamps. Checks older than 36 hours are marked overdue. A later transcript does not make an older interview new. Questions before you start Are the views verified? Reviewed views retain original sources and verified chapter times when available. Automatic discovery contains source metadata, not reviewed claims. Attribution does not establish truth. Does Jarvis predict the future automatically? It currently provides source-linked editorial guidance and action starting points. It does not generate AI probabilities, truth scores or personal assessments. What is free, and what does membership buy? Reading, original videos, local records and exports are free. Existing AGI membership adds cloud workspaces and version history, not automatic personal-report subscriptions. Will saved views send me notifications? No. You can keep local records, choose a review date and export a calendar entry. Cloud storage does not imply automatic alerts. Find my question ↗ (/future-guide)

## 模拟环境中的成功，能迁移到真实工作吗？ | AGI

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/zh/future-guide/simulation-gap

## Jarvis — turn an AI goal into a useful next step

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/jarvis

Give Jarvis a research goal. Get source-linked findings, practical next steps and a private task history. Try one task free, then register a free AGI account to continue. Shared usage limits apply.

Q: How does the free trial work?
A: Guests can submit one task, then register a free AGI account to continue. A saved task uses the trial even when AI is unavailable. Reading, exporting and deleting its result remain available. An interrupted first run can resume saved work, but a new run or daily watch needs an account. One trial is recorded per browser key; the same IP can start at most one guest trial in 24 hours. This is abuse prevention, not verified identity: shared networks may need to register sooner. Registration uses the existing AGI display name and private login-key backup, with no email, payment or extra model quota.

Q: What can Jarvis do today?
A: Research AI work, learning and product ideas using our editorial catalog. With your choice, it can search GitHub and Hacker News metadata. It can calculate, compare findings and draft concrete next steps. It cannot control your computer, access your accounts, send messages or buy things.

Q: Does it continue when I leave?
A: Submitted tasks are stored on the server. A background runner checks the queue about every two hours; scheduled checks can be delayed. After free registration, daily watch runs up to seven times over seven days; results appear here, with no email or push notifications. You can pause or delete a task. Resuming an interrupted run reuses saved steps; a model call with an unknown outcome is not silently repeated. The guest trial can finish in the background; further runs need free registration, not a paid membership. Previously paused tasks need an explicit resume.

Q: What happens when AI is unavailable?
A: You get the matching source pack and an explicit limited status. No preset is passed off as AI output. A new run gathers evidence with code and uses one synthesis call; an older checkpoint can total two calls. It shares the existing site allowance of 12 attempts per 24-hour window and 3 per IP window. Failed attempts count too.

Q: Where are my goals and memories stored?
A: Editable memories stay in this browser; only the relevant memories you select are sent with a task. Submitted tasks and their selected context are stored in Cloudflare D1 for 30 days and sent to Workers AI for inference. Enabled public searches send only your explicit public search keywords to GitHub or Hacker News. A private key saved in this browser protects task access; clearing it can lose access. Existing member keys still open their original task history, even after membership expiry. Device memories are separated by workspace. Do not submit sensitive data. Delete a task to remove it from our active store. A separate minimal trial receipt (workspace hash, task identifier and date, without task text) is retained to prevent resetting the trial by deletion or expiry. Network-limit hashes expire after 24 hours and are removed during bounded maintenance. Choosing registration and continuation links this browser’s trial history to your account; device memories can move with it. It does not publish tasks to the discussion room.

Q: Is this AGI, and is it a paid product?
A: No AGI capability has been established. This bounded research-agent pilot is free, with one guest trial followed by free account registration. No paid membership is required. There is no separate Jarvis plan. Shared model and search limits still apply, and availability is not guaranteed. We are testing whether people find these results useful and return with real tasks.

---

## 贾维斯 — 把 AI 时代的目标推进一步

URL: https://agiscorecard.com/zh/jarvis

交给贾维斯一个研究目标，获得有出处的发现、可检验的行动和私有任务记录。先免费试用一次，再注册免费 AGI 账号继续使用，受共享额度限制。

Q: 免费试用与注册有什么限制？
A: 访客可提交一个任务，之后免费注册 AGI 账号继续。保存任务即占用试用机会，AI 不可用也计数；已有结果仍可查看、导出和删除。首次任务中断可接续已保存步骤，新一轮运行或每日跟踪需要注册。每个浏览器密钥记录一次试用，同 IP 每 24 小时最多开始一次访客试用；这是防滥用措施，并非实名识别，共享网络可能需要提前注册。注册复用 AGI 昵称与私有登录密钥备份，无需邮箱或付款，不增加模型额度。

Q: 现在可以做什么？
A: 可以检索站内 AI 工作、学习与产品观点；经你选择后，可检索 GitHub 和 Hacker News 的公开元数据。支持算术、比较发现与制定下一步。当前不能控制电脑、访问你的账户、发消息或购买商品。

Q: 关闭网页后会继续吗？
A: 提交的任务会保存到服务器，后台约每两小时检查队列，调度可能延迟。免费注册后，每日跟踪最多运行 7 次，持续 7 天；结果在这里查看，暂无邮件或推送通知。你可以暂停或删除任务。中断后恢复会复用已保存步骤，结果未知的模型调用不会自动重试。访客试用可在后台完成，后续运行需要免费注册，不要求付费会员；此前暂停的任务需要你主动恢复。

Q: AI 额度不足时怎么办？
A: 保留匹配的资料包，并明确标记受限状态，不把预设文案冒充 AI 输出。新任务由代码取证，只调用模型综合一次；旧版检查点续跑累计最多两次。与站点共享现有每 24 小时窗口 12 次、每 IP 窗口 3 次的额度；失败也计数。

Q: 目标与记忆保存在哪里？
A: 可编辑的记忆保存在本浏览器，只把你勾选的相关记忆随任务发送。提交的目标和所选上下文在 Cloudflare D1 保存 30 天，并发送给 Workers AI 推理。开启公开搜索只会向 GitHub 或 Hacker News 发送你明确填写的公开关键词。本浏览器保存的私有密钥保护任务访问，清除密钥可能失去访问。原会员密钥仍可打开原任务历史，会员到期也不影响使用。本机记忆按工作区分别保存。请勿提交敏感资料。删除任务会移除活动数据库中的记录。独立的最小试用凭据仅保留工作区摘要、任务编号和日期，不含正文，用于防止删除或到期重置试用。网络限额摘要 24 小时后失效，并由有界维护清理。选择注册并接续时，会将本浏览器试用历史关联到你的账号，本机记忆也可随之迁移；任务不会发布到讨论区。

Q: 这是 AGI 吗，需要付费吗？
A: 尚未证明具备 AGI 能力。这是有边界的研究 Agent 试用版，提供一次访客免费试用，之后需注册免费账号继续，不要求付费会员。不另售贾维斯套餐，仍受共享模型与检索额度限制，不保证随时可用。我们正在检验这些成果是否有用，以及用户是否会带着真实任务回来。

---
